topic.title: Juniper Hierarchical IS-IS Routing (L1, L1/L2, L2 BNG/PE/P)

tier.function: Maintains L1 LSDB only. Establishes L1 adjacencies to L1/L2 Aggregation routers. Relies on the Attached (ATT) bit default route (0.0.0.0/0) generated by L1/L2 Aggregators for core/BNG reachability.

Connects L1 access domains to the L2 core backbone. Sets the ATT bit in L1 LSPs to provide default routing to L1 nodes. Leaks specific L2 routes (like BNG loopbacks) down into L1, and advertises L1 access prefixes up into L2.

tier.nodes: BNG Nodes, PE Routers, P Routers
tier.function: Core backbone area. BNGs operate strictly as L2 nodes, establishing L2 adjacencies to L1/L2 Aggregators and L2 Core P/PE routers. BNGs inject subscriber pools, framed routes, and pseudowire (ps*) interface subnets into Level 2 IS-IS and MP-BGP.

bngIsisRoutingMode.description: Since BNGs reside in Level 2, they communicate with Access Switches indirectly through L1/L2 Aggregation nodes. Traffic from L1 Access switches reaches the L2 BNG via the L1/L2 Aggregator's default route or specific leaked L2 routes.

keyRequirements.item: BNG interface connections to Aggregators must be configured for Level 2 only (`set protocols isis interface <interface> level 1 disable` or `level 2-only`).
BNG loopback (lo0) and subscriber access pseudowires (`ps*`) must be advertised in L2 so PE routers and Aggregators can resolve BNG subscriber traffic.
Wide metrics (`wide-metrics-only`) must be enabled across all tiers (L1, L1/L2, L2) to ensure high-bandwidth metric calculations for BNG routes remain consistent.

workflow.title: Access Switch (L1) cannot reach BNG (L2) Loopback or Subscriber Gateway
workflow.step: Check L1 default route on Access Switch: `show route protocol isis 0.0.0.0/0`. If missing, verify if L1/L2 Aggregator is generating the ATT bit in its L1 LSP.
Check ATT bit on Aggregator: `show isis database detail | match "Attached bit|Heading"`. If ATT bit is not set, the Aggregator lacks active L2 adjacencies or L2 routes to the BNG.

If specific BNG routes (e.g. BNG loopback or subscriber pool) are required in L1 instead of default route, verify L2-to-L1 route leaking policy on the L1/L2 Aggregator: `show configuration protocols isis level 1 export`.
Check BNG L2 database entry: `show isis database l2-extensive <BNG-System-ID>` to confirm the BNG is originating its loopback prefix into L2.

workflow.title: BNG (L2) cannot reach Access Switch (L1) Management IP
workflow.step: On the BNG, query the route: `show route <access-switch-ip>`.
If missing, check if the L1/L2 Aggregator is summarizing/redistributing L1 prefixes into L2 IS-IS.
On the L1/L2 Aggregator, verify the L1 prefix exists in the L1 database (`show isis database l1-extensive`) and that L1-to-L2 propagation policy is active.

workflow.title: BNG Pseudowire (ps*) or Subscriber Pool Unreachable from Core PE
workflow.step: Verify BNG L2 adjacency status: `show isis adjacency` (confirm Level 2 Up state).
Check if BNG is injecting subscriber prefixes into IS-IS L2: `show route protocol isis | match ps` or `show route advertising-protocol bgp <peer-ip>`.
Verify recursive next-hop resolution on the receiving PE: `show route <subscriber-prefix> detail` to ensure the BNG's L2 loopback is valid and reachable in `inet.0`.

A route being active in IS-IS/inet.0 does not guarantee Layer 2 resolution. Verify ARP/subscriber binding on the PE/BNG itself: `show arp no-resolve interface ps<N>.<unit>` — see routing/arp.xml's bngSubscriberResolution section for the PE/BNG candidate device list (197.155.94.100, 197.155.94.138, 41.175.38.42, 41.175.38.43) and the ps-number-equals-unit-number rule.
